title: A continuous range of dip rates fits eight years of CPV flags without a zero-rate star class
abstract: We test whether persistent complex periodic variable (CPV) flags require a separate class of host stars. We use 8,772 TESS sectors of 1,746 neighbour-clean M dwarfs from a verified SCI publication. A model with a fixed positive duty in every star, drawn from a beta distribution per age class, fits the flags with log likelihood -632.875 using 9 parameters. The published changing-host model gives -632.042 with 10 parameters. A discrete permanent-host model gives -636.916 with 9 parameters. Five-fold tests by star give a continuous-model log-score gain of 7.723 over permanent hosts, with a descriptive bootstrap interval of -6.817 to 25.514. Both models pass a coarse count check. A minimum duty of 0.0001 in every star costs almost no likelihood; a minimum of 0.01 costs 27.2 log units. The age decline remains. A covariance calculation and a coupling bound show how lasting rate differences can mimic a fixed host class. Material replacement rates do not enter the flag likelihood, so these flags alone cannot set a grain lifetime. This does not refute the source correlation-time bound within its host model. It limits the use of that bound to exclude short repeated supply events. The continuous duty law is assumed, and source labels and detection efficiencies are not remeasured. Code, hashes, aggregate results, and a figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Continuous and discrete rates, minimum-duty sensitivity, and count checks for the released TESS flags. The distribution curves are fitted models without confidence bands. The count bars show 95% simulation intervals.
